If you are putting Semgrep, ZAP, sqlmap or PyRIT behind an LLM orchestrator and using the system prompt for everything, this paper shows some of the problems you will encounter.

So what changes should be in the pipeline then?

1. Make sure runs do not fail silently. Long-lived sessions lose resident evidence over time, so pass artefacts and not the whole conversation. Short-lived sub-agents writing schema-validated summaries extend the usable horizon by the compression ratio.

2. CLI-easy ≠ pipeline-easy. The following is ok to put in the pipeline without much changes: Gitleaks, Semgrep, Playwright, sqlmap (hard-cap it). For others like ZAP and promptfoo, a wrapper to fix their deficiencies would likely be needed.

3. the LLM/AI can't be where you put your entire "trust" on.

4. Don't record “could not score” as “attack failed”. More details in evaluation is definitely needed to improve the pipeline.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21423
